value.headline: Early voting numbers show a shift toward Democrats. If those hold, two House seats in Virginia could flip, and a third could be close.
value.claim: Early vote up in Democratic localities, down in Republican ones; State Navigate sees EV 6.5 pts more D in VA-01, 5.9 in VA-02, 4.7 in VA-05 vs 2025
value.cmp: 2026 vs 2025 (same point), locality raw counts; State Navigate model
value.evidence: Comparison is like-for-like in time (same point, prior year) and the author flags the 2025 blue baseline and that VA has no party registration. As of the snapshot statewide EV was 3.7% behind 2025; by 10/23 it was 10.3% ahead (VPAP day 11: 999,454 vs 906,418) [V]. Locality-level 2025 counts not re-measured here (VPAP WAF challenge).

rows.source: Cardinal News (Dwayne Yancey): Early voting numbers show a shift toward Democrats. If those hold, two House sea
rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.headline: Early Voting Numbers Soar Across Virginia
value.claim: Almost twice as many early votes as the same time four years ago; in VA-05 and VA-06 more people voted by 10/20 than voted early in all of 2022
value.cmp: 2026 vs 2022 same point; 2026 partial vs 2022 final by CD
value.evidence: VPAP day 11: 999,454 vs 561,443 in 2022 = 1.78x [V]. CD data: VA-05 109,809 vs 90,889 final 2022; VA-06 93,906 vs 74,897 [V]. But the same CD table shows Republican-held/leaning CDs (5, 6, 9, 1) ahead of their 2022 finals while NoVA Democratic CDs (8, 10, 11) are behind theirs: the surge is not concentrated in D areas. 2022 is a weak baseline (pre-adoption); vs 2024 same point 2026 is 32% lower.

rows.source: The Daily Signal (Rich Tucker): Early Voting Numbers Soar Across Virginia
rows.note: The verdict is our like-for-like reading of the claim (grade I); the evidence cites its own grades.

value.headline: With Two Weeks of Early Voting Left, Where Are We in Virginia at This Point?
value.claim: VA early vote 60D-36R vs 55D-40R at this point in 2024: 9 points bluer
value.cmp: modelled party (a commercial voter file) 2026 vs 2024 same point
value.evidence: Like-for-like modelled comparison by the modeller [R]. VoteHub primary-history split 28.2% leans D vs 18.2% leans R (53.6% unclear) [R]; caveat: Republicans held no statewide 2025 primary, which inflates D primary history. Morris himself translates it to about 3 pts of margin vs 2024, not 9.

value.headline: Early voting surges in battleground states as Democrats outpace GOP gains
value.claim: Nearly 930,000 Virginia early ballots through Thursday; early voting concentrated in districts where Republicans are playing defense
value.evidence: Total is right (VPAP day 12: 933,925) [V]. "Concentrated where Republicans play defense": VA-01 and VA-05 are the two largest CD totals, but VA-06 and VA-09 (safe R) are also above their 2022 finals; NoVA D districts lag. Concentration in R-held districts is equally consistent with Republicans now voting early.
